htmlContent:
How to Reduce Missed Calls in Your Small Business

Missed calls have the potential quite literally to be a silent killer, and you know as much. It is a cost to any small business by losing customer trust and hitting the wallet, and that is just for the important calls; forget the nightmare of the game of phone tag.

It is a world out there these days, and each call in it could be another sale. Today's sales managers should not let an important call go unanswered.

This article will explore the problem of missed calls in some depth, looking at average customer value and customer retention in the context of specific busy periods when call tracking is imperative.

  • Their costs are not just at the cash register but can be measured in calls missed, alerts, and the sales lost as a result, hence the importance of the phone in every return call.

  • Possible causes of missed calls that are (more) common in e-commerce companies are: long waiting period, poor handling of either one or different kinds of calls, and an old traditional telephone system.

  • A few simple ways you can prevent a missed call and make sure your business always responds quickly are by putting missed call alerts in place, ensuring all your lines are as clear as possible, getting extra operators in at busy times, and making sure someone picks up as soon as the phone rings.

Understanding Missed Calls and Their Impact

The Cost of Missed Calls for Business Owners

To small business owners, every missed call isn't a trivial inconvenience; missed opportunities and lost revenues are even more so when calls go unanswered.

It's not just a missed interaction; a missed call sets in motion a cascade of events that affects several areas:

  • A customer who is trying to contact a competitor may be calling during a busy period when your team is swamped and isn't able to pick up the call.

  • The volume of missed calls and value per customer also affects sales calls and overall profitability for an e-commerce business; the busier the phone is, the more it affects the business.

The total number of missed calls rapidly translates into serious financial loss. Therefore, service businesses, in general, and all small businesses should utilize a reliable missed call solution.

Common Reasons for Unanswered Calls

Reasons for unanswered calls on an e-commerce business are diverse; they are easily rectified, and could contribute to a reduction in the average customer value.

During peak hour use, the multitude of incoming calls to the call center can often be too much for the staff to handle, resulting in much of the inbound call traffic being sent to the voicemail facility or often being missed altogether.

Another issue is the after-hours inbound call traffic, where there are often no human operators present to talk to the customer, and the callback misses the mark entirely, which has a significant impact on call tracking.

Causes of these slumped callback times include waiting time and mismanaged types of calls, which could result in a loss of customer interaction.

  • If there are not enough staff members, an important opportunity may be missed, and therefore, call tracking becomes even more crucial.

  • Poor Call Handling Processes can result in Missed Call Alerts and Customer Dissatisfaction; a system needs to be implemented to handle different types of calls on a day-to-day basis effectively.

  • The business operates in the e-commerce world. A broken phone system can negatively impact it, with missed call alerts going up and customer status decreasing. This is essential during peak hours, when the phone is ringing everywhere.

All those factors result in a bad customer experience, and – what really matters – lost revenue for your business, in particular if callers who can't get to you pick up your competitors. (This makes things worse from a call tracking perspective.)

Impact on Sales and Customer Satisfaction

The immediate damage would be a missed sale. Still, a missed call has longer-term effects on the average customer value, the business reputation, and the ability to return the call.

A missed call will have a huge negative impact on the e-commerce customer's perception of the reliability of your e-commerce business and also the business’s professionalism, so you need to answer the call.

This then becomes a determinant of whether the customer/client is happy with your service as a business. This could make your clients go to a competitor for those later appointments because of the long wait for a response, meaning loss of today’s sale, but future sales and advertising via word of mouth.

The great missed call would mean that business owners lose those appointments and those future bookings and effective word of mouth feedback, particularly if the call was a crucial appointment, meaning that the missed calls on behalf of small e-commerce businesses contribute to the general broken down trust of potential customers.

Effective Call Solutions for Small Business Owners

Implementing Call Management Technology

For small business owners, investing in state-of-the-art call management systems will be one of the most effective ways to dramatically reduce the number of missed calls and deliver an even better customer experience.

The sophisticated phone systems have proved to be reliable enough to handle unpredictable call volume with ease, and smart enough to make sure no calls are left unanswered.

Through AI-enabled call solutions, companies can create the perfect setup to answer callers’ questions, directly connect calls to the right agents and departments, and even introduce an AI agent to handle common inquiries during busy times or after hours, so no outbound opportunities are missed, a problem that leads to the loss of revenue.

Utilizing Call Forwarding to Answer Calls Promptly

For any small business, a call forwarding solution is essential if they wish to look busy but actually be free still to answer those crucial sales calls or customer queries.

Call forwarding allows an incoming call to be rerouted (via the original company's landline/mobile) when no one is available to answer it, the call can be redirected to a colleague or friend/partner that can help, to a mobile, or to a virtual receptionist service, thus massively reducing missed call alerts.

Whether a business uses the call forwarding option simply on their main landline or has to re-route multiple lines, it is a simple but effective missed call solution, in keeping customers happy and keeping that missed call from becoming a missed call alert.

Voicemail Best Practices to Prevent Missed Calls

While an overall objective for an e-commerce business would be to have no missed calls, it is not always possible to avoid situations where a call will be diverted to a voicemail system, – this could be due to the volume of incoming calls or out of normal business hours.

In order for an e-commerce business to offset potential damage resulting from not being able to take a call, voicemail best practices should be in place so that the customer is encouraged to call back.

In order to minimize the damage to the customer relationship, the business owner should ensure that the caller receives clear, concise, professional messages indicating when they will be available to return the call and an alternate method of contact if applicable.

Calling the customer back promptly (see above) indicates to the customer that a proper, responsive service has been provided, no matter how disappointed they may be that you were not able to answer their call – it could take as little as this to make an e-commerce business successful.

Leveraging AI to Reduce Missed Calls

AI Agents as Your First Line of Communication

AI is changing the way small business owners receive incoming calls in that it can be the fastest, most comprehensive solution to missed calls, equipping business owners to handle their customer calls efficiently and enhancing call setup.

An AI agent can take responsibility for a large percentage of incoming calls, especially when a business is busy or closed, helping to make sure that no important calls are missed.

Such sophisticated, proactive AI can handle most basic questions by automatically answering phone calls to collect caller details, or even raise a ticket with the business, alleviating the need for people to have conventional phone setup, and helping to significantly cut down on missed calls so users can continue to answer only those calls that they care about, while making sure that callers who cannot get through are called back quickly with no missed opportunities.

Call Patterns and AI Insights for Better Management

Using AI in an e-commerce application cannot only help businesses answer calls, but it can also help managers get insightful data on call behaviors and call traffic.

Small business owners or call centers can utilize call management solutions to send all call logs straight to their sales or customer service team, providing them with valuable business intelligence on call history, peak time, customer questions, and even why an e-commerce call may be missed.

Knowing this information helps e-commerce sales and service teams maximize staffing, refine call handling protocols, and build more efficient call routing practices.

Through intelligent call management, small business owners can understand their call traffic and anticipate solution needs, and then move to answer every call and prevent missing calls from potential customers or clients.

Call tracking can be made smarter through the use of an intelligent missed call solution.

How AI Phone Systems Can Help Your Sales Team

An AI phone system can be the difference your sales team needs to slash missed call alerts and missed opportunities, saving them time on the call and improving the number of calls per day when a customer is interested.

An AI Agent automates initial caller screening and qualification to be sure your sales line is only “touching base” with the most qualified callers, avoiding wasted time on unqualified callers, and expediting successful sales.

Business information, such as past conversations or caller history, can be instantly reported back to your sales team from an AI agent so they can enhance the call with account-specific details and increase conversion rates.

This will make it easier to track missed calls and help qualify and convert every single call into a sale.

Strategies to Stop Missing Calls After Hours

Setting Up After-Hours Call Solutions

To stop your business from missing calls after business hours, small business owners need to have the ability to provide after-hours call options.

A dedicated phone system can be set up to run during off-hours, so that at least every call is answered and can no longer receive the dreaded missed call alert.

These options can be in the form of an automated solution, which can handle common questions, provide basic information, or transfer callers to an emergency contact number.

Any number of sophisticated call handling solutions use AI to transfer emergency calls to on-call personnel or provide callback options.

This extra step can stop phone tag and unused opportunities. An e-commerce business can stop missing these opportunities by ensuring every call gets answered.

Automated Responses for After-Hours Inquiries

Automated responses are another solution for the after-hours missed calls problem.

This also provides a way of giving callers an immediate response, letting them know that someone in your business has acknowledged their call.

An AI agent, or an AI voice agent, can be configured to cater to several after-hours calls that perhaps have a simple answer, or can be directed elsewhere on the internet, or perhaps take their information and call back during regular business hours.

This will not only make sure that everyone who calls up gets a response, but also leave a positive experience with the customer, so that they feel after-hours business calls are also being attended to. The customer isn't being left hanging to feel as if they got no answer.

This could effectively cut the number of after-hours missed calls for any small business to ensure no loss in revenue.

Balancing Availability and Personal Time

Finding a healthy balance between business availability and time is the major challenge for small business owners.

Call centers can greatly help small business owners to avoid burnout while not missing any calls.

They can implement a call management system or even an AI call answering system that would be able to handle inbound calls; the calls after hours may be responded to much faster, and the calls would be pre-sorted so that the call center would only need to handle the high-priority sales calls or customer service needs.

This way, all their calls would be answered, and they would not have any of their staff overworked, increasing customer satisfaction and improving quality of life for small business owners, and helping them to stay within their marketing budgets.

An e-commerce business that does not want to miss calls uses a smart solution.

Best Practices for Small Business Owners

Tracking and Analyzing Unanswered Calls

For small business owners, routinely tracking and analyzing missed calls is a must to discover where there is room for improvement and get a true grasp on the bottom-line cost of every missed call (in marketing spend).

State-of-the-art phone system solutions today can generate call logs and analytics that can show you exactly when most missed calls are hitting your business, why they are missed, and possibly even what your potential customer profile looks like.

With this critical analysis of missed call data, businesses can then understand where the pitfalls are, and what timing during the day results in more missed calls than they can handle, and develop a strategy to actually STOP missing calls to ensure they are not losing business to a competitor, by analyzing call data.

Common Questions to Address with Your Team

In order to be successful at meeting the challenge of missing fewer calls, small business owners need to be willing to involve their staff in talking about the repetitive questions around when, how, and why we handle calls the way that we do.

They need to question themselves, “Why did this call take place, and why did we miss it? And who can we assign to answer these calls more effectively and reduce missed call if we give our call center the ability to track the call?” or “What can our small business do to make sure we are answering every call and tracking every missed call more effectively now, with improved setup and call tracking?”

Obtaining help and advice from others in the business to answer questions that revolve around the proper mechanism of Callback procedures for after-hours calls, how to operate and use the call forwarding more efficiently, and ways to implement voicemail best practices from the most effective may be the key to significant success.

Creating a Culture of Responsiveness in Your Business

Developing a culture of responsiveness may be the most effective business best practice for small businesses to stop missing calls and keep customers happy and engaged, reducing the potential for phone tag.

A culture of responsiveness is more than a new phone system; it starts with setting a goal that every call is a priority and that missing a call could mean the difference between a growing business and a missed opportunity.

Effectively training human operators to use the phone system efficiently and successfully, encouraging skilled operators to call all voicemails immediately, and proactively conducting call log reviews with the team to highlight victories and devise additional improvements will help small businesses grow.
